chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUthmān, from Ismāʿīl ibn Jābir, who said:
I sought permission from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام while we were fasting in Ramaḍān, to go and meet Walīd at al-Aʿwaṣ. So he said: Meet him and break your fast.
So the proper understanding of this report is that it pertains to a state of taqiyyah and fear, not to a state of choice.
ai.seo_question: How is a hadith about breaking the fast in Ramaḍān during travel understood in a situation of taqiyyah and fear?
ai.summary: This report concerns the ruling of fasting during travel in Ramaḍān and records an instruction to break the fast when going out to meet someone. The closing clarification states that this instruction is to be understood in a circumstance of taqiyyah and fear, not as a general ruling in a normal state of free choice.
